title: Purpose, reason and result
tagline: Why you did it, why it happened, and what happened because of it — three different sets of linkers.
exam: Reading & Use of English Part 4 — key word transformations
Reading & Use of English Part 2 — open cloze
Writing Part 1 — essay: cause and effect
why: Essays and reports need to explain why something is done (purpose), why something happens (reason), and what the consequence is (result) — and B2 First expects three different sets of linkers for these, not one all-purpose 'because'. The fixed patterns so...that, such...that and too/enough are especially common in Part 4.

rows.label: Linkers
cells: to / in order to / so as to / so that
because / as / since / because of / due to / owing to
so...that / such...that / as a result / therefore

rows.label: Followed by
cells: infinitive, or a clause with so that
a clause (because/as/since) or a noun (because of/due to)

rows.label: Example
cells: She left early so as to catch the bus.
The match was cancelled due to the storm.
It rained so hard that the match was cancelled.

diagrams.title: so ... that / such ... that
diagrams.caption: She was so tired that she fell asleep in class.

diagrams.title: too / enough
diagrams.caption: He's too young to vote in the school elections.

head: Function
Pattern
Example
rows: She saved money to buy a new phone.
so as to / in order to (+ not)
He whispered so as not to wake the baby.
so that + can / could / will / would
Leave early so that you won't be late.
Because it was raining, we stayed in.
because of / due to / owing to + noun
The trip was cancelled due to bad weather.
It was so cold that the match was postponed.
It was such a cold day that we stayed in.
It snowed heavily; as a result, school was closed.

use.point: Purpose: explaining why you do something

examples.text: Nadia joined the debate club to improve her public speaking.
Miss Vega spoke slowly so as to make sure everyone understood the instructions.
examples.note: so as to, slightly more formal

examples.text: Take a jacket so that you won't get cold on the way home.
examples.note: so that + will/won't for a future purpose

examples.text: Because the internet was down, the class had to reschedule the test.
The final was postponed due to the terrible weather in Cusco.
examples.note: due to + noun, common in formal writing

examples.text: Since most students already knew the topic, Miss Vega skipped the introduction.
The exam was so difficult that half the class ran out of time.
It was such a difficult exam that the teacher gave everyone extra minutes.
The instructions were too confusing to follow without help.
Mateo wasn't confident enough to raise his hand.
examples.note: enough goes after the adjective, before the infinitive

examples.text: The bridge was closed for repairs. As a result, traffic built up across the city.
Attendance had been falling for months; therefore, the club changed its meeting time.

watch_out.wrong: We stayed home because the rain.
watch_out.right: We stayed home because of the rain. / We stayed home because it was raining.
watch_out.why: Because needs a full clause; before a noun you need because of, due to or owing to.

watch_out.wrong: She ran so as she wouldn't miss the bus.
watch_out.right: She ran so that she wouldn't miss the bus.
watch_out.why: So as to is only followed by an infinitive; a clause with a modal needs so that.

watch_out.wrong: It was such cold that we cancelled the match.
watch_out.right: It was such cold weather that we cancelled the match. / It was so cold that we cancelled the match.
watch_out.why: Such needs a noun (such cold weather); with just an adjective, use so.

watch_out.wrong: He was too tired to studying.
watch_out.why: Too + adjective is always followed by a to-infinitive, never -ing.

watch_out.wrong: She isn't enough old to drive.
watch_out.why: Enough goes after the adjective, not before it.

watch_out.wrong: The concert was cancelled, due to the storm damaged the stage.
watch_out.right: The concert was cancelled because the storm damaged the stage. / ... due to the storm damage.
watch_out.why: Due to takes a noun, not a clause with its own verb.

dialogue.title: Why the sports day was cancelled
dialogue.context: Sofia and Mateo are explaining to Nadia, who was absent, why the school sports day didn't happen.

lines.speaker: Sofia
lines.text: It was cancelled because of the storm — the field was completely flooded.

lines.speaker: Nadia
lines.text: Seriously? It rained so hard that they couldn't even open the gates?

lines.speaker: Mateo
lines.text: Exactly. The ground was too wet to walk on, let alone run a race.

lines.speaker: Sofia
lines.text: Miss Vega checked the field early so as to decide before everyone arrived.

lines.speaker: Nadia
lines.text: Good thinking. Since the buses were already booked, what happened to those?

lines.speaker: Mateo
lines.text: They used them anyway, so that nobody would waste the trip.

lines.speaker: Sofia
lines.text: We went to the sports centre instead — it wasn't big enough for everyone, though.

lines.speaker: Nadia
lines.text: It was such a chaotic morning that half the year didn't even find out in time.

lines.speaker: Mateo
lines.text: True. As a result, they're rescheduling it for next month.

lines.speaker: Sofia
lines.text: Good — I trained for weeks to win the relay this year.

items.sentence: The trip was cancelled ___ the bad weather.
Nadia left the party early ___ she wouldn't miss the last bus.
items.why: so that + clause with a modal (wouldn't)

items.sentence: It was ___ noisy in the hall that nobody heard the announcement.
The instructions were ___ complicated to follow without an example.
Liam wasn't fast ___ to catch the bus in time.
___ she had studied every topic, Sofia still felt nervous.
items.why: since = because, giving a reason clause

items.sentence: The stadium roof was damaged in the storm. ___, the concert was moved indoors.
items.why: as a result links two full sentences

practice.instructions: Complete each sentence with the correct word or phrase.

items.sentence: Mateo woke up early ___ (in order/get) to the airport on time.
___ (because/the) traffic, the bus arrived twenty minutes late.
The lecture was ___ (so/boring) that half the audience left early.
It was ___ (such/a) difficult question that nobody answered it correctly.
The bag was ___ (too/heavy) to carry up the stairs alone.
She wasn't tall ___ (enough) to reach the top shelf.
Ticket sales fell sharply; ___ (therefore), the festival was shortened to two days.
He whispered the answer ___ (so as/not) to disturb the rest of the class.

practice.instructions: Complete the second sentence so that it has a similar meaning to the first. Use the word given. Do not change it. Use between two and five words.

items.first: The road was closed because there had been an accident.
Sofia practised every day because she wanted to improve her Spanish.
The music was extremely loud, so we couldn't hear each other talk.
items.second_end: we couldn't hear each other talk.

items.first: Nadia is not experienced enough to lead the project on her own.
items.second_end: to lead the project on her own.

items.first: There was a power cut, so the whole street lost internet access.
items.second_end: the whole street lost internet access.

items.first: He locked the door quietly because he didn't want to wake anyone.
items.second_start: He locked the door quietly so as

summary: Purpose (why you do it) uses to, in order to, so as to, or so that + clause.
Reason (why it happens) uses because/as/since + clause, or because of/due to/owing to + noun.
Result (what happens because of it) uses so + adjective + that, such (a) + noun + that, or as a result/therefore between two sentences.
Too + adjective + to-infinitive means 'more than necessary'; enough goes after the adjective, before the infinitive.
Because of and due to need a noun, never a clause with its own verb.
